text: Git branching is a key part of modern version control workflows. When developers work on new features, they create separate feature branches instead of changing the main code directly. This keeps the main branch stable while work is in progress. Once a feature is finished and tested, it can be merged back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open a pull request so others can review the changes, discuss them, and suggest improvements. This workflow helps teams collaborate safely, catch mistakes early, and keep the project organized. Understanding branching makes it much easier to work with others on the same codebase.
